anomalies.description: A dark sedan in the left lane loses control, swerves right across the lane line, and slides sideways into the flooded right shoulder/embankment, kicking up a large spray of water and debris.; The same vehicle remains overturned or heavily tilted on the right shoulder, partially submerged in floodwater; it appears stationary or slowly drifting downstream as water flows around it.

A vehicle on the right shoulder/snowbank loses control, slides sideways, and appears to spin or roll partially, kicking up snow and debris; it remains off-road and damaged through frame f6 (7.0s), with visible motion blur and disturbance consistent with a crash.

A second vehicle (light-colored, possibly white or silver) enters the scene from behind, approaches the accident site, and appears to slow or stop near the disabled vehicle on the flooded shoulder; its headlights are visible and it remains in proximity through the end of the clip.

At timestamp 11.5s (f15), a multi-vehicle collision is clearly visible: a dark sedan is stopped directly behind two large trucks in the same lane, with visible proximity and deformation suggesting impact; debris is airborne and other vehicles are involved in a chain-reaction crash.

A white box truck on the right shoulder loses control, swerves sharply left across the emergency lane and into the adjacent traffic lane, colliding with or narrowly missing the silver sedan in front of the camera vehicle.

A dark SUV in the left lane (visible from f14) appears to lose control or brake suddenly, causing a rear-end collision with the black car directly behind it; debris is visible and the black car’s rear is pushed upward at impact.; A dark-colored sedan on the right side of the highway is struck from behind or sideswiped, causing its rear to swing sharply left and its roof to visibly crumple inward. Debris is ejected.; The same sedan remains severely damaged with a collapsed roof and misaligned rear end, continuing to travel slowly in the right lane while other vehicles pass. The damage is consistent and persistent across frames.

A vehicle with headlights is visible approaching on the road at f0; by f1, the explosion occurs at approximately the same location, suggesting the vehicle was involved in or proximate to the initiating event (e.g., collision leading to explosion). The rapid onset and location imply a crash-triggered event.; A vehicle on the right side of the road appears to lose control and veer off, resulting in a bright flash and large plume of dust/snow, consistent with a crash or rollover.

A sudden, intense bright flash erupts on the right side of the road, rapidly expanding into a large luminous cloud with visible shockwave-like propagation and debris/steam dispersion, consistent with a high-energy explosion.
